Brand book · v2.1 · 22 Oct 2026

Know where to stop.

This is Zyflow's visual identity: how the brand looks and sounds on every surface we make. That means the app, zyflow.eu, the web planner, emails, social posts, ads, share images and decks. Use it whenever you design for Zyflow or show Zyflow in your own materials: the team, designers, agencies and partners.

3 typefaces1 green action1 orange moment1 route blue

Logos and colour values are in Downloads. Questions about using the brand: support@zyflow.eu.

01 · The idea

A guidebook for riders

Zyflow is a guide to places, not a route app. It shows riders where to stop: stays, coffee, food, chargers, water and repair, and what makes each one welcome a bike. Every surface we make should read like a page from one well-made guidebook.

Paper

Every page is sand paper. Content sits directly on it, separated by space and thin hairline rules. No cards inside cards, and never a page in pure white.

Pictures

Maps and photographs are the book's illustrations. They are square or full-bleed, with no frame and no rounded corners.

Data

Distances, counts and times are set in mono. A plain fact stated precisely does more for us than an adjective.

  • FeelConfident, outdoors, premium, calm.
  • OneOne headline, one green action, one orange moment per surface.
  • RealReal roads, real places and real numbers. Slovenia first.
  • GenerousNew areas have little data, so the design has to look complete with only a count, a type and a distance.
  • NeverGlass effects, gradient buttons, dark-first layouts, dashboards, cards inside cards.
  • NeverEmoji, illustrated heroes, 3D blobs, purple-to-blue gradients.
  • NeverTwo saturated colours fighting on one surface.
  • NeverCentre everything, stock smiles, or "Discover Amazing Routes!"
02 · Logo

Mark and wordmark

  • Clear spaceOn every side, keep a gap the height of the mark's top bar, about 20% of the mark's height (the dashed outline above).
  • Min sizeMark 16 px; wordmark 72 px wide. Below 16 px, use the favicon PNG.
  • PlacementTop-left or bottom-left on social posts and share images; top-left in emails. Small: the logo signs off a composition, it doesn't headline it.
  • Filesdesign-system/assets/logos/
  • Don'tRecolour the orange swash, or swap the green and orange.
  • Don'tPlace the colour logo on a saturated colour field (green or orange). Use the cream on-dark version.
  • Don'tStretch, rotate, outline, add shadows, or retype the wordmark in a font.
  • Don'tUse the mark as a map pin. Pins show place types.

04 · Type

Three faces, three jobs

Display
Tanker · uppercase · −1%
Every stop. One map.
Figures
Tanker · tabular
134 KM
Reading
DM Sans · 400/500/600

Stays, coffee stops, restaurants and chargers, each one showing what makes it bike-friendly. Free on iOS and Android.

Data
Courier Prime · caps +4%
Ljubelj pass · 26 km · +900 m · Alpine
  • OneOne display size per surface. The headline is the only thing in Tanker, apart from one big number.
  • ShortA Tanker headline is 7 words or fewer. Uppercase makes long lines hard to read.
  • MonoMono means "you are reading data". Eyebrows stay on one line and never wrap.
  • LeftAlign left. Centre only a single short line in a hero.
  • Don'tSet a sentence in mono, or a number that matters in DM Sans.
  • Don'tSubstitute a serif. It reads as a different brand.
  • Don'tUse Inter, Poppins, Montserrat, Work Sans or Google Sans. All retired.
  • Don'tFake bold or italic Tanker. It has one weight.

Files: design-system/assets/fonts/. Tanker is under the ITF Free Font License (Fontshare); DM Sans and Courier Prime are OFL and on Google Fonts. Where Tanker can't load (some email clients), fall back to Impact, "Arial Narrow Bold", sans-serif, never a serif.

05 · Signature devices

Four things only Zyflow does

Every strong set in the galleries had one or two recurring devices that made it recognisable without the logo: Vita Coco's colour fields, Corporate Traveler's highlighted phrase, Margin's mono voice. These are ours. Use at least two in every marketing piece.

1 · The map window

A square or full-bleed crop of the calm map: route blue on a white casing, a green start dot and a flag at the end. No radius, frame or drop shadow. It is the one picture every area has, even where we have no photos. Generate it with the map kit or the route-card worker, never by hand.

Featured route
Ljubljana to Trieste
134 km+1,766 m1 day

2 · The data strip

Mono caps between an ink rule and a hairline, with values divided by hairlines. It is the caption for every route, place and stat. Use 3–4 values only, and always real ones.

Stop where your bike is welcome.

3 · The highlight

One phrase of a Tanker headline set in a green block with white type. For ads, social posts and deck statements only, never in the product UI. One per headline. It counts as the surface's single green, so it can't sit next to a green button.

New · Kamničanka route is live

4 · The orange dot

Outside the logo, orange appears only as one small dot or ring: "new", "live" or "selected". Because it is that rare, it always reads as signal and never as decoration.

On zyflow.eu only

The website has three devices of its own, kept for its warmer, hand-made feel. Use them on the website and nowhere else: not in the app, emails, ads, social posts or decks.

  • PolaroidsA small collage of real photos in white frames, slightly tilted, with a soft shadow. At most one collage per section, real places only.
  • Torn paperA torn-paper edge where one sand band meets another. It replaces the hairline between whole sections, never inside one.
  • CornersPhotos, maps and cards on the website take a 12 px corner. In the app and every other format, pictures stay square.
06 · Imagery

Real roads, early light

  • WhereSlovenia first, then the country the content is about. Name the place in the caption.
  • PlacesShoot the stop as well as the road: a café terrace with bikes leaning on it, a charger by a guesthouse door, a water fountain.
  • CropSquare or full-bleed. Text on a photo goes only over the hero scrim, at the bottom. On zyflow.eu only, photos may take the 12 px corner (see §5).
  • PeopleReal riders with permission, named in stories (see §8). Seen from behind or small in landscapes.
  • Don'tUse stock smiles, faces looking at the camera, brand logos on kit, or AI-generated scenes.
  • Don'tAdd rounded corners, frames, polaroid tilts or drop shadows to photos in the app, emails, ads or social posts. Polaroids belong to the website only.
  • Don'tUse tight full-UI screenshots. Show one phone screen, large, or crop the UI so it bleeds off the edge.
  • Don'tUse HDR, heavy vignettes or teal-and-orange grading.
07 · Voice

Plain, specific, second person

WriteNotWhy
Know where to stop.Discover amazing routes!A verb first, a plain promise, no exclamation mark
Every stop. One map.The ultimate all-in-one cycling platformShows the benefit instead of naming a category
134 km · +1,766 m · chargers placed for your batteryEpic long-distance adventureA number beats an adjective
Nothing bike-friendly here yet · Add the first oneNo results foundAn empty state is a sentence plus an action
Kamničanka is live →🚀 BIG NEWS!!! Check out our new featureThe news first, then the link. No emoji
  • Headline7 words or fewer, sentence logic, ends with a full stop.
  • ClaimDeck and ad titles state a claim, not a topic: "Chargers placed before you need them", not "Battery features".
  • One verbOne call to action per surface: Get the app · Explore nearby · Ride this route · List your place.
  • SlovenianInformal ti, same plainness. Other languages follow the English meaning, not a literal translation.
  • ReasonsShow the reason: "not confirmed yet", "nobody has confirmed bike parking".
  • CaptionsOne plain sentence plus a number or a credit. At most two hashtags: #zyflow and the place.
08 · Proof

Real numbers, named people

The social-proof gallery comes back to one point again and again: proof only works when it is specific and checkable. A small team showing real numbers comes across as more confident than a big claim.

8
Countries live

Impact metric: one big Tanker figure plus a mono label. Only numbers the app shows today.

"I planned the coffee stops before the climbs. That's the whole point."

Name Surname · Kranj → Kamnik · 70 km

Rider story: a quote with a real name and the route they rode. Placeholder shown; never invent one.

Free · iOS and Android · Made in Slovenia

Microcopy next to the main button: three short facts that are true. Add the store rating once it is worth showing.

  • NeverUnattributed quotes, rounded-up vanity numbers ("10k+ riders" before it is true), logo walls of companies we don't work with, or stock-photo testimonials.
09 · Templates

One frame, many stories

Every channel uses the same few frames. The best ad and social sets in the research kept the frame fixed and changed only the content. Do the same: copy a frame, swap the data, and keep the positions.

Social posts
Paid ads · one series, three angles
Share images (Open Graph)
Website announcement bar
Transactional email
  • CanvasSand #F9F8F4 edge to edge, with a 560 px column and 32 px padding. Content sits on the sand. No white card and no card inside a card.
  • HeadWordmark at 104 px, top-left. Mono eyebrow. Tanker headline from the web font, falling back to Impact, never Georgia.
  • CodeCourier Prime bold 34 px, letter-spaced, on one recessed band. When a link is needed instead: a green pill, 48 px tall, white label naming the action.
  • FooterMuted #71717A at 14 px, never lighter. Why you got this email, plus support. Security emails have no social icons and no promotions.
  • Subject45 characters or fewer, no emoji: "Confirm your Zyflow email".
  • Dark modeKeep color-scheme: light. Test the Gmail and Outlook forced-dark views; the logo PNG needs a cream keyline.
Deck · 16:9 · four layouts

12 · Before you export

Checklist

The background is sand, not white.
One Tanker headline, 7 words or fewer, uppercase.
One green element at most, and it is the action or the highlight.
Orange only in the logo plus at most one dot.
Route lines are blue on white casing, from the map kit.
Every number is real, and set in mono or Tanker figures.
Photos are square or full-bleed, with no radius and no orange grade.
Text on photos sits over the hero scrim.
The logo is the right version for the ground, with clear space.
Copy is plain, second person, no emoji, one call to action.
It reads at 500 px wide.
It uses the template's frame unchanged; only the content differs.
